CPUAFFINITY - the row now says that an unset variable stops the instance. The basis is systemd.service(5) (the `${NAME}` form always gives one argument, empty when the name is unset) and the `taskset` parser, which rejects an empty CPU list. It was not run under systemd here. One start of `rinzler@N` on a test host with no `CPUAFFINITY` line in the instance file, followed by `systemctl status rinzler@N`, would settle it.

POS_1GB_PER_NUMA, POS_NR_HUGEPAGES - the rows now say that a count of 0 hugepages stops the process at startup. The basis is the code path (`mmap_file()` with a size of 0 bytes, then `TRON_ASSERT(store != MAP_FAILED)` in src/system/huge.cpp) and mmap(2), which gives EINVAL for a length of 0. It was not run. One start of a hardware test program with `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES=0` on delphi-3b35 would settle it.

POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH - the row now says that an empty value fails startup. The basis is the code path: `scan_hugepage_dir()` opens the parent directory of an empty path, the open fails, the cleanup returns false, and `pos_heap_setup()` returns -1 (src/system/huge.cpp:260, src/system/memory.cpp:149). It was not run. One start of a hardware test program with `POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH=` (empty) would settle it.

HWATTN_WLR - what an FPGA card does when the variable forces reuse on and the bitfile fails the check (hwattn_wlr_bitfile_ok). The driver sends the reuse commands without a check, and the code does not show the result on the card. A run on a card with an older bitfile, or a statement from the bitfile owners, would settle it.

TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH - which request first ends the process with a negative value. The code ends it at the first token add to a tree node whose parent is not the root (std::vector::reserve of a size above max_size inside the noexcept defrag_books). When a workload first reaches such a node was not measured. A run of two requests that share a prefix, with the value -1, would show it.

TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR - the outcome of text without a number on the second code path. On the main path std::stof throws inside the noexcept kv_location_for_tokens, which ends the process. create_children also calls requested_num_pages for an append larger than one allocation, outside a noexcept function, and its callers were not traced. A run of such an append with the variable set to a word would show it.

TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING - the code does not show what a forced ON does on a bitfile that fails the check (wrong results, a stall or an error). The bitfile check only names two FPGA fixes (h/pos/device.hpp:797). A run on a bitfile older than 05.09, or a statement from the FPGA team, would settle it.

TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT - what a person sees with the value `0`. The code shows that the prompt position does not advance (src/tron/generation/context.cpp:74) and that an add of 0 tokens puts the request callback on the unchanged node (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:516, src/tron/scheduler/full.cpp:192). Reading suggests that the request never finishes, but no line proves it. One run of `runtron` with the value `0` on a test host settles it.

TZ - whether `TZ` also moves the time of day in every log line of `rinzler` and `runtron`. The log pattern prints `%H:%M:%S` (src/system/spdlog.cpp:69) and `set_pattern` is called without a time type. The spdlog documentation gives local time as the default, but the checkout holds no spdlog source to confirm it. The `set_pattern` declaration in the spdlog header of the version that the build uses settles it. If confirmed, the row needs one more sentence, and `runtron` in "Read by".

RZ_RUNFILE_DIR - whether a program outside this repository (for example platformd) reads `/var/log/positron/rinzler-<pid>.run` on a deployed system. The repository holds only test readers (t/t_rinzler.cpp:291, t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py:42). The platformd source or its owners settle it.

TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE - whether the output of the abort holds the text `Failed to load Harmony encoding`. The code path says no: the `harmony_error` is not caught, and the terminate handler logs only backtrace lines (src/common/backtrace.cpp:33). t/proxy/README.md:457 says that the proxy fails with that text. One start of `rinzler_proxy` with a gpt-oss model and `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE=/nonexistent` settles it.

TRON_TOKENIZE_PY - what the process does when the program exists but exits with an error. `make_python_tokenizer` logs `Failed to create fallback python tokenizer` and returns a tokenizer without a handle (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:1927). `tokenizer::encode` then uses the handle without a test (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:310). One run with `TRON_TOKENIZE_PY=/bin/false USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER=1` shows the result. The row does not state this case.

TRON_LOG_DIR - where a production instance writes `alderaan.log`. The packaged unit does not set the variable, and its working directory is `/opt/positron`. The tron-host drop-in says that the `positron` user cannot write there (packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf:9). Whether platformd sets `TRON_LOG_DIR` is not in this repository. One read of `/etc/rinzler/instance-<N>.env` on a deployed host settles it.

RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH - the row says that `rinzler` aborts when the mount fails. This comes from the code path (src/rinzler.cpp:4988 is outside the try block). No run confirmed it. One start of `rinzler` with `RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH` under a directory that the user cannot write settles it.

RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED - what platformd does when the mount moves to /var/run/rinzler/<N>/instance-<N>. The unit file says in a comment that the platformd statistics scanner then fails, but platformd is not in this repository. The platformd source or a test on a deployed system would settle it. The row states only the path change, which the code shows.

PERFETTO_PRODUCER_SOCK_NAME - the socket that the Perfetto SDK uses when the variable is unset. The SDK is not in the repository. The row gives the two paths that perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh expects. The Perfetto source of the pinned version (GetProducerSocket) would settle it.

DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH - Which launchers give pytest a first argument named pytest under /.cache/uv/ (the third accepted form in _cmdline_is_pytest, bin/dice:328-331). The row states the code rule only. Reading /proc/<pid>/cmdline of a pytest process started by 'uvx pytest' or 'uv tool run pytest' would settle which launchers pass.

DICE_RUNTIME_DIR, DICE_SOCKET_PATH, DICE_STATE_PATH - The statement that bin/slice stops on a shared host comes from reading the call path (bin/slice:951-952, 5543, 7105-7109), not from a run. Running 'DICE_RUNTIME_DIR=/x bin/slice queue' on a shared host with a live daemon would confirm the printed text.

CABAL_INSTALL - The row says that CMake searches the name `cabal` before the value of the variable. This follows from how CMake handles `ENV CABAL_INSTALL` after `NAMES` in find_program (ingest/CMakeLists.txt:260): CMake puts the value in the argument list at that place, so it becomes one more name. The checkout does not show this CMake behavior, and the CMake manual describes `ENV` only after HINTS and PATHS. A configure run with `cmake --debug-find-variable=CABAL_EXECUTABLE` and CABAL_INSTALL set to a second cabal would settle it.

GHC - how CMake treats `ENV GHC` after `NAMES` in `find_program`. The row says the value is one more candidate name, tried after the fixed names. This is behavior of CMake itself (the argument parser in its source file `cmFindBase.cxx`), not of the checkout. A configure run with `cmake --debug-find` and a test value of `GHC`, or that CMake source file, would settle it.
GHC - what `cabal run` does with an empty `-w` value (the Empty case of `build-model.py`). A run of `cabal run ingest -w ""` would settle it.

TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS - what `subprocess.run(pass_fds=...)` does with a number that is not an open descriptor. The row keeps the general sentence. A short Python experiment outside the repository would settle it.

RUN_COVERAGE - the statement that the default ID `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` is not in the model list of `build-all.sh`. It was derived by reading `get_ingest_list` and by parsing `config/models.yaml` with the same filter in a scratch script. The repository command `python3 config/model_definitions.py --registry config/models.yaml --list-ingest` was not run. Its output would confirm it.

start_address - whether a bash newer than 5.1 still reads `0x` with no digits as 0. The row says that an unset variable gives the base address on the first pass. A standalone snippet with the arithmetic line of bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh:15 confirmed this on bash 5.1.16 only. Running `bash -c 'echo $((0x))'` on a lab host with a newer bash settles it.

PAUSE_LEN_NS - whether a larger value lengthens the measured wait on an Intel CPU. The code passes a length in cycles as the absolute TSC deadline of `tpause` (t/t_mwaitx.cpp:808, src/system/mwaitx.cpp:91), so the deadline is expected to be in the past. A run of `PAUSE_TYPE=tpause PAUSE_LEN_NS=<value> gen/t_mwaitx "[pause]"` with two values, compared on the printed average wait, would settle it. No test was run here.

TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH - what `rinzler_proxy` does when the value is empty and the test starts it without `--model-path`. The row states only that the option is left out (t/t_rinzler_proxy.cpp:1062). Reading the start-up path of `src/rinzler.cpp` for a run with no model option, or one run of the test with an empty value, would settle it.

REMOTE_BUILD_MEM - the unit that the lab LSF installation applies to the number in `rusage[mem=<value>]`. The script prints the number with the suffix M and README.md:519 says MB, but the repository holds no LSF configuration. The LSF configuration of the lab cluster, or the `bjobs -l` output of one build job, settles it.

INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION, TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION - what `uv` does when the value is empty and `--python` gets no version. The rows say only that `--python` gets no version. One run of `uv sync --frozen --python` in a scratch project settles it.

NPROC_BUILD - what GNU make does with text after `-j` in MAKEFLAGS that is not a number. The row says only that the makefile does not check the text. One `make NPROC_BUILD=abc list-tests` run settles it. Running make in the checkout was not allowed here.
REMOTE_BUILD_CORES - which GNU make versions show `-jN` in MAKEFLAGS only inside recipes. The makefile code handles both cases. The version numbers come from README.md:521 and were not tested.

CLANG_RESOURCE_DIR - which program `flake.nix` sets it for. No file in the repository reads the name, and the repository names no outside reader. The commit that added the line (7783df0511, `git log -S CLANG_RESOURCE_DIR -- flake.nix`) or its author can settle it.

CMAKE_C_COMPILER - whether a program of the Nix dev shell reads the environment variable. No file in the repository reads it. To my knowledge CMake takes the C compiler from the environment variable `CC` and has no environment variable `CMAKE_C_COMPILER`. The CMake manual page cmake-env-variables(7) settles it.

SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED - the new last sentence of Effect says that `True` or `TRUE` makes the health check expect `2x72core`. The repository shows only the expression `vars.SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED == 'true'` (.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml:43). That `==` ignores letter case for text comes from the GitHub Actions documentation (page 'Evaluate expressions in workflows and actions', section Operators), which was not opened in this check. Remove the sentence if that source is not accepted.

SLICE_REFRESH_ROLLOUT_ENABLED - whether text in another letter case, for example `TRUE`, passes the job conditions. The conditions use the workflow expression `== 'true'` (.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml:48). The GitHub Actions documentation of expressions says that string comparison ignores letter case. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` compares the exact text (bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh:74). If the documentation holds, `TRUE` starts a scheduled run that then fails in job `plan`. The repository code cannot settle this. One workflow run with the variable set to `TRUE` settles it. The row is unchanged on this point: it tells the reader to set the exact lower-case text.

APT_DEPLOY_KEY - what the shared workflow `positron-ai/github-actions/.github/workflows/publish-apt.yml` does with an empty `SSH_PRIVATE_KEY`. The workflow is not in this checkout. Its source at the pinned commit 5af69f7a settles it. The row states the unset behavior only for the step of `publish-deb.yml` that this checkout holds.

SLICE_REFRESH_ALERT_ASSIGNEES, SLICE_REFRESH_REVIEWERS - the exact list form of the value (commas between names, team names as reviewers). The script passes the text unchanged to `gh`, so the repository code does not define the form. The `gh issue edit` and `gh pr edit` manual pages settle it. Both rows keep the pointer to the `gh` option.

PYTHON_VERSION - what `uv sync --python` does when the variable is unset. The option then gets no value or an empty value. The repository does not show the result. A run of `uv sync --python ""` with the pinned `uv` would settle it. The row only says that no default exists.

EXPECTED_RUNNER_CLASSES - whether one `2x72core` runner lacks the `benchmark` label, as the glossary hint says. The runner list in the GitHub settings would settle it. `bin/ci/bench_refresh_matrix.py:19` asks for the `benchmark` label for both classes. The new rows do not depend on this fact.

TEMP, TMP - whether the rows should also name the indirect readers. Python `tempfile` (for example bin/dice-lsf-runner:433, bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py:285) and `std::filesystem::temp_directory_path()` in the test programs (for example t/fuse_test_env.hpp:31) read TMPDIR first and then TMP and TEMP. That order is library behavior that the checkout does not show. The source of the Python and C++ standard libraries in use would settle the order. The owner of the document decides whether indirect reads belong in these rows, as they do in the LNAME row.

AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY - whether the GitHub Actions runner program or the image of the hosted runner defines the name. The checkout only reads it (.github/workflows/nix-build.yml:87). The runner-images repository of GitHub settles it. The cell keeps 'GitHub Actions'.

XDG_DATA_HOME - the sentence about saved approvals rests on Nix behavior, not on Tron code: Nix keeps the approvals of flake `nixConfig` settings in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/nix/trusted-settings.json`. The Nix manual (option accept-flake-config) or the Nix source confirms it. The checkout supports it only through the comment at .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml:146.

ImageOS - why the workflow still sets it. No Tron file and no step script reads the name. The line was added in commit be14ba38b1 when the workflow used the action erlef/setup-beam, which is gone now. The source of the four actions that the workflow uses today (checkout, upload-artifact, find-comment, create-or-update-comment) at their pinned commits would show whether one of them reads ImageOS.

CCACHE_CONFIGPATH, CCACHE_DIR - whether the value of the preset `base-ninja` replaces a caller value in `cmake --preset <name>` and in `cmake --build --preset <name>`. The rows say only that the preset sets the path. The CMake manual cmake-presets(7) says that a preset sets each variable of its `environment` map also when the process environment already holds a value. No run was allowed here. One run of `CCACHE_DIR=/tmp/x cmake --build --preset native` followed by a look into `/tmp/x` settles it.

CXX - which program uses the value that the workflows `cmake-single-platform.yml` and `benchmark-golden.yml` set. No Tron file reads CXX there, and the CMake presets set `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` themselves. Candidates are the build tools of the dependencies, for example Meson and cargo build scripts. The configure and build log of one CI run with CXX removed settles it.

CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM - the sentence about CMake 4.x rests on the CMake documentation of this variable, not on Tron code. The repository holds only the assignment of `3.5`. The CMake manual page of `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM` is the source.

LDFLAGS - which link commands of the Tron build inside the Nix dev shell get `-lgcc_s` from this variable. The Linux CMake presets set `CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS`, `CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS` and `CMAKE_MODULE_LINKER_FLAGS` themselves (CMakePresets.json:25). The CMake documentation says that CMake reads `LDFLAGS` only to give these variables their first value. The row therefore states no effect on the Tron build. The link lines of `ninja -v` in a new build directory inside the Nix dev shell settle it.

GHCRTS - the order in which the GHC runtime applies its options (the built-in `-with-rtsopts` text first, then `GHCRTS`, then the command line) comes from the GHC User's Guide, not from repository code. The guide section on the `GHCRTS` environment variable settles it, or one run of the built `ingest` program with `GHCRTS=-N4 ... +RTS -s`, which prints the thread count in use.

MAKE - whether a `MAKE` value from the environment replaces the value that GNU Make gives the variable itself. The row says only that the recipes run the command in `MAKE`, which holds in both cases. One run of `MAKE=echo make -n format`, or the GNU Make manual on the origin of `MAKE`, settles it. Running make in the checkout was not allowed here.

NIX_NO_SELF_RPATH - the checkout holds no reader, so the sentence about the run path rests on nixpkgs behavior that was not read here. Source that settles it: `pkgs/stdenv/generic/setup.sh` (function `_addRpathPrefix`) and `pkgs/build-support/setup-hooks/multiple-outputs.sh` at the nixpkgs revision that `flake.lock` pins. If that source differs, cut the second sentence of the last cell.

OMP_NUM_THREADS, OMP_THREAD_LIMIT - the rows describe `nproc`, not Tron code. The behavior was measured with GNU coreutils 8.32 on the agent host only. Measurement that settles it for the build hosts and the Nix dev shell: `nproc --version` and `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=2 nproc` there.

OMP_THREAD_LIMIT - who sets it. Only a makefile comment (GNUmakefile:93-94) says that LSF sets it to the reserved cores. No code in the checkout sets it, so the row does not say it. Measurement that settles it: `env` inside an LSF job on the lab installation.

HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy - whether the file transfers of `huggingface_hub` that go through the `hf_xet` library (a second download client, written in Rust) also use the proxy. The rows claim only the API requests, which go through `httpx`. The source of the locked `hf_xet` release would settle it.

GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS - which software defines the name, and whether any program reads it. No code in the checkout reads it. The binaries of git 2.34.1 and CMake 3.22.1 on the audit server do not contain the string. A search of the current git source for the name (git grep GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS in git.git) would settle whether a newer git reads it.
